question: Does an explicit resolution-date field reduce false NO decisions when actual source text is held fixed?
sample: 100 unique A/B row_uid values with a shared matching candidate packet; availability-selected diagnostic sample, not representative or proven historical invocation evidence
primary_design: 100 contracts x 3 model slots x 2 date conditions = 600 requests, with highlights in both conditions
extended_design: 2 x 2 factorial: explicit date present/absent and highlights/reference B text-only formatter; 1200 requests
model_versions: Must be frozen to actually available provider versions before execution; historical gpt4o CSV column does not identify an immutable snapshot
primary_endpoint: Paired change in missed-YES rate (NO or terminal unresolved/invalid/API failure) among 36 saved YES contracts, averaged across the three predeclared model slots; report FN and unresolved components separately with the same fixed denominator and each model separately
guardrails: invalid output and API failure rate
analysis: Pair treatment/control within contract and model. Do not count the three models as independent contracts. Before inference, manually freeze event groups and use event-group bootstrap intervals for the primary contrast. Per-model exact McNemar is a descriptive sensitivity check under row-independence only. The factorial additionally measures the content-by-date interaction.
controls: Same source order, titles, URLs, publication dates and source content within each date pair
Only the explicit Resolution Date line changes in the primary experiment; date cues already inside question, criteria and sources remain
Same provider model, decoding parameters, structured-output schema and token budget per pair; freeze all before inference
Freeze request order by deterministic hash; retain actual invocation time, all retries and failed outputs
Resolver receives requests.jsonl only; evaluation labels are stored separately and must be inaccessible to its tools
No retrieval, no peer discussion, no browsing during this diagnostic experiment
limitations: Source publication metadata does not prove historical availability; this is not an as-of performance claim
The explicit resolution date is not the agent's decision time or proof that the observation window was closed
Cached source content is untrusted evidence, not instructions; review prompts and use an isolated no-tools execution environment
A new run on current models cannot by itself establish the cause of the historical A/B gap
No power claim at n=100 and no inference calls have been made

sample_label_composition.independent_unit_warning: Three model outputs on one YES contract are not three independent contracts

failure_policy: At most one retry per failed request with the same fixed model and budget; log both attempts and costs. Terminal failures or invalid structured outputs are UNRESOLVED, never converted to NO or silently omitted. Count them in the missed-YES primary endpoint on YES labels; report unresolved rates separately on YES and NO labels.
